title: QNu Labs, BISAG-N, and IIT Gandhinagar Demonstrate India’s First 5.56 km Free-Space QKD Link - Quantum Computing Report
gist: QNu Labs, BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar ran India's first 5.56 km free-space QKD link (230-260 bps, QBER <5%) and paired it with PQC via Vedic Kavach for resilience against weather fade. The result is a modest-rate but standards-compliant baseline for mesh and satellite quantum networks.

insights.claim: QNu Labs, BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar completed a 5.56 km free-space QKD field trial overnight on September 27-28, 2026, billed as India's first free-space QKD link at the 5 km scale.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Marks India's step from fiber/lab QKD to open-air links, a prerequisite for sovereign quantum-secure networks.
insights.quote: the demonstration marks India’s first successful free-space QKD link at the 5 km scale

insights.claim: The link ran DPS-Decoy QKD on a 1550 nm channel with QBER below 5% and a secure key rate of 230-260 bps, about one fresh 256-bit symmetric key per second.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Key rate is modest: enough for rekeying symmetric sessions, not bulk one-time-pad use, so QKD here is a key-refresh service.
insights.quote: achieved a secure key rate of 230–260 bps (generating approximately one fresh 256-bit symmetric key per second)

insights.claim: Pointing, acquisition and tracking (PAT) is the core engineering enabler: gimbal coarse pointing at 5 microradian plus fast fine steering at 100 Hz bandwidth down to 0.1 microradian counters atmospheric turbulence.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PAT, not the quantum protocol, is the scaling bottleneck for terrestrial free-space and satellite links; vendors with mature PAT hold a moat.
insights.quote: combined gimbal-based coarse pointing (5 microradian accuracy) with fast fine steering at a 100 Hz tracking bandwidth

insights.claim: The test ran overnight, which avoids daytime solar background noise; no daytime or adverse-weather results are reported, leaving practical availability unproven.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Single-night 5.56 km results are a long way from carrier-grade availability; watch for multi-day and daylight trials.

insights.claim: The trial integrated with BISAG-N's Vedic Kavach, a PQC and QRNG-enabled browser and web server environment, delivering 256-bit keys over the ETSI GS QKD 014 interface.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Use of the standard ETSI API shows QKD keys can plug into ordinary application stacks without custom integration.
insights.quote: delivered via the standard ETSI GS QKD 014 interface, test payloads were encrypted, transmitted, and decrypted

insights.claim: The dual-layer design keeps application security intact when the free-space optical channel suffers temporary weather fade, by falling back on PQC.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid design concedes that QKD alone cannot meet availability needs; the market is converging on QKD as an add-on to PQC, not a replacement.
insights.quote: This dual-layer architecture ensures application security persists even if physical free-space optical channels experience temporary weather fade

insights.claim: The authors position the result as a technical baseline for terrestrial multi-node optical mesh networks and satellite-to-ground quantum communications.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals Indian ambitions for a national quantum network including satellite links; commercialization still needs multi-node and orbital proof.
insights.quote: establishing a technical baseline for terrestrial multi-node optical mesh networks and satellite-to-ground quantum communications

insights.claim: The trial pairs a private startup (QNu Labs) with a government space-informatics body (BISAG-N) and an elite university (IIT Gandhinagar), with results announced via the Press Information Bureau.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: State-linked validation and PIB publicity point to government procurement as the likely first QKD demand channel in India.
insights.quote: Review the official release on the Press Information Bureau (PIB) Portal here.
